document_manifest.note: The back-matter glossary (शब्दसूची) is a HIGH-VALUE pre-existing pronunciation resource: it gives Marathi term + English term + a phonetic Marathi transliteration of the English pronunciation for ~150 technical terms. This should be ingested directly as a seed for the pronunciation-risk lexicon rather than re-derived, per spec section 25's caution against inventing Romanized phonetics.

cross_chapter_class8_science_grammar.common_pattern_across_book: Nearly every chapter opens with 'थोडे आठवा' (recall box, prior-grade knowledge) and/or 'सांगा पाहू' (discussion prompt), interleaves 'करून पहा' (hands-on activity/experiment) and 'जरा डोके चालवा' (reasoning prompt) throughout the body, and closes with स्वाध्याय. This 'recall -> activity-driven concept building -> स्वाध्याय' template is COMMON across all 19 chapters (pattern_scope: COMMON) — structurally similar to History's template but activity-centred rather than narrative-centred, matching spec's expectation (§10) that subject grammar differs meaningfully by subject even within one board/grade.
recurring_boxed_element_types: करून पहा (hands-on activity/experiment — THE defining Science-chapter element, present in all 19 chapters, often multiple per chapter)
माहीत आहे का तुम्हांला (enrichment fact box, very frequent)
इंटरनेट माझा मित्र (internet-research prompt, excluded from normal narration)
हे नेहमी लक्षात ठेवा (key-fact/summary box, occasionally safety-critical)
सोडवलेली/सोडविलेली उदाहरणे (worked numerical examples — concentrated in CH_03, CH_14, CH_16, the more mathematical chapters)
परिचय शास्त्रज्ञांचा / असे होऊन गेले / मागे वळून पाहताना (scientist-biography or history-of-science vignette, appears in CH_03, CH_10, CH_11, CH_18 — GENRE_SPECIFIC, used to humanize discovery)

historical_model_sequence_chapters: CH_05 (अणूचे अंतरंग — uniquely presents 4 sequential scientist/model pairs)

cross_chapter_class8_science_grammar.pronunciation_risk_density: Dense but differently-shaped than History: fewer personal names overall, but very high density of technical/scientific terminology (chemical compound names, taxonomic terms, physics units) plus a real mix of scientist names (many non-Indian: Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr, Archimedes, Golgi, Harvey, Landsteiner). The book's own back-matter glossary (शब्दसूची, pdf pp.145-146) already gives ~150 term-pairs with phonetic transliteration and should seed this lexicon directly rather than being re-derived from scratch.
cross_chapter_class8_science_grammar.narration_policy_pattern: Body prose -> READ_THEN_EXPLAIN (default). करून पहा activity instructions -> READ_DIRECTLY (procedural, should be read as literal step-by-step instructions, not summarized). सोडवलेली उदाहरणे (worked numerical examples) -> READ_THEN_EXPLAIN but REQUIRE a distinct mathematical_narration speaking style (state 'दिलेले'/given values, then formula, then substitution, then answer — never collapse to prose). इंटरनेट माझा मित्र / माहिती मिळवा (research prompts) -> EXCLUDE_FROM_NORMAL_READING, these send the student to an external search rather than containing narratable content themselves. Safety-warning content (never taste unknown chemicals CH_12, never add water to concentrated acid CH_12, fire/earthquake dos-and-don'ts CH_09) -> flagged IMMEDIATE spoken_priority regardless of surrounding chapter's general narration policy, since this is life-safety information.

speaking_style_taxonomy_for_this_subject.used_for: concept/definition/property prose — the dominant style for most chapters

worked numerical examples and formula derivations — CH_03, CH_14, CH_16 specifically need this as a first-class distinct style per spec §18/§20's requirement not to treat mathematical expressions as ordinary prose
करून पहा hands-on activity steps — imperative, numbered, safety-annotated where relevant
brief vignette boxes only (CH_05 model-history, CH_10/CH_11 scientist bios, CH_18 term etymology) — a minority mode within Science, unlike History where it's dominant

chapter_specific_exceptions: CH_05: uniquely structured as a sequence of four historical scientific models (Dalton->Thomson->Rutherford->Bohr), each with its own evidence and limitation — closer to History's narrative-arc pattern than to the rest of Science's activity-driven pattern. CHAPTER_SPECIFIC / possibly a bridging pattern worth flagging for cross-subject grammar comparison.

CH_09: contains genuinely life-safety-critical content (earthquake/fire dos-and-don'ts) that should override the chapter's general narration policy with IMMEDIATE priority for those specific passages.

CH_12: contains two explicit safety warnings (never taste/smell/touch unknown chemicals; never add water to concentrated sulfuric acid) that are SAFETY_CRITICAL and should be flagged IMMEDIATE regardless of general chapter policy.

CH_02: contains a case-study paragraph (Gaurav, a child from a poor family with an alcoholic father) requiring careful, non-judgmental narration tone — similar sensitivity handling to History's treatment of poverty/hardship content.
CH_08: contains the Bhopal gas tragedy (real mass-casualty industrial disaster, ~8000 deaths) — requires the same measured, non-dramatized delivery flagged for History's violence/tragedy content.
CH_17: contains real health-hazard content about thermocol/styrene (carcinogenicity, leukemia/lymphoma risk) — factual, non-alarmist tone needed.
CH_18: the 'Divija and the bee sting' reasoning scenario briefly uses narrative/empathy-building framing atypical for the rest of the chapter — worth preserving rather than flattening.

HIGH_RISK: All chemical formulas, equations, and numerical worked-example arithmetic across CH_03/05/06/07/12/13/14/16 — must be checked against the rendered page since OCR/extraction of subscripts, superscripts and special characters (₂, ⁻, etc.) is unreliable and was visibly imperfect in raw extraction (e.g. some formulas showed spacing artifacts)

MEDIUM_RISK: narration_policy and speaking_style assignments (AksharSetu recommendations, not textbook facts)
structural_pattern discovery per chapter (SUPPORTED_INFERENCE from heading/activity order)
Safety-critical content flagging (IMMEDIATE priority assignments) — the flagging logic itself should be human-reviewed given the stakes of getting this wrong

Given Science's exceptionally high diagram density (especially CH_01, CH_05, CH_10, CH_11, CH_16, CH_19) and its many chemical/mathematical formulas that OCR handles unreliably, a page-rasterization + visual-verification pass is even more important here than for History before any narration/TTS is generated.
